turns: I have an interview for the PhD Intern role at Figma on Thursday. prep me
replies:
Good — we'll prepare exactly for the PhD Intern (AI Applied Scientist) interview at Figma on Thursday. I ran a brief on the role and their process and built a focused prep plan. Do the items below now; I’ll draft your answers and run a timed mock when you say “mock me for PhD Intern at Figma.”

Assumptions I made (sensible defaults):
- Interview length: 45–60 minutes.  
- You want a concise, interviewer-ready set: 60s Tell-me-about-yourself, 3 STAR stories, 3 behavioral answers, 2 smart questions, and one product+technical example tied to Python/Go/ML.  
- Results in stories should include a numeric outcome; I left numbers as [number] where you must provide them.
What I prepared for you now
1) Short prep checklist (do these before Thursday)
- Re-read the posting (they list python, go, machine learning, product).  
- Prepare one concrete example that shows production ML work (data, model, deployment), one example showing Go or systems engineering, and one showing Python/data-science scripting.  
- Prepare slides or 1–2 Figma frames for a project deep dive (record suggests project deep dive in Figma).  
- Confirm interview time, time zone, link and interviewers; test audio/video and screen-sharing a day before.  
- Print/watch Figma product surfaces and frame your technical answers in product terms (collaboration, real-time editing, scaling).
2) 60-second "Tell me about yourself" — draft (edit the bracketed bits)
"I’m [Name], a PhD candidate in [field] at [university], where my research has focused on [research area — 2–3 words]. I build end-to-end ML systems: for example, I designed a [model/type] to [task], training on [data type], which improved [metric] by [number or percent]. I’ve shipped research into production twice: I wrote the data pipeline in Python, trained and evaluated models, and integrated the service with a Go backend for low-latency inference. I enjoy working on product-focused ML problems that directly affect user experience — I want this Figma PhD Intern role because it’s where applied ML meets product and scale, and I can contribute both research depth and production experience."
Fill in: [Name], [field], [university], [research area], the concrete project specifics and numeric result.

3) Three STAR stories (short templates — fill specifics and numbers)
- Team win (collaboration)
  Situation: [project context].  
  Task: My role was [role].  
  Action: I coordinated across [teams], introduced [method/process], implemented [feature/experiment] using Python and a Go-backed API; I prioritized reproducible pipelines and clear metrics.  
  Result: Outcome was [quantified result: e.g., reduced latency by X ms, increased metric Y by Z%], shipped in [weeks/months].
- Hard technical problem (depth + technical choices)
  Situation: [hard problem].  
  Task: I needed to [goal].  
  Action: I experimented with [algorithms/models], built a scalable training pipeline (Python + distributed tooling), optimized inference with a Go service and caching, and validated with an A/B test.  
  Result: Achieved [number], and the solution scaled to [users/requests per sec].
- Failure / learning (growth + feedback)
  Situation: [project that failed].  
  Task: My responsibility was [role].  
  Action: I made a wrong assumption (state it), we missed [impact]. I owned the fix: I restructured data validation, added unit tests and a small offline evaluation suite, and redesigned the deployment checklist.  
  Result: After the fix, we reduced regression risk and improved release time by [number]; I learned [concrete lesson about process or design].
4) Three behavioral Qs to practice (and how to answer)
- “Tell me about a time you gave/received difficult feedback.” — Use STAR; emphasize how you adjusted work and kept relationships. End with the measurable improvement.  
- “Describe a time you had to prioritize conflicting product and research goals.” — Show trade-offs, where you leaned product-first or research-first and why, and the resulting user impact.  
- “Tell me about a time you disagreed with a teammate.” — Show respectful conflict, data-driven decision, and final compromise plus outcome.

I’ll score answers and give one concrete improvement when you do the mock.
5) One technical-product example they want (matches the record)
- Example to use: a product-framed ML project where you solved a user-facing problem (e.g., suggestion/embedding/ranking/collaboration feature). Structure: problem → user impact → model choices → dataset → offline metrics → deployment architecture (Python training, Go inference) → A/B or monitoring → result (numbers). Keep it short (2–3 minutes) and have a slide/frame showing architecture and a result graph.
6) Two smart questions to ask them
- "What does success look like for a PhD Intern on this team after the internship?"  
- "What are the biggest technical or product challenges the team expects to tackle in the next 6–12 months?"

7) Interview-stage notes (from the brief)
- Official early: likely an initial recruiter or hiring manager screen — be ready to succinctly state your fit and confirm logistics.  
- Engineer: expect medium-difficulty coding/system design and a project deep dive in Figma; have code examples ready and a short demo or Figma frames for your project.
Next actions I can do for you now
- Draft complete, word-for-word versions of the Tell-me-about-yourself and the three STAR answers using your specifics (I will need your project names, role, numbers).  
- Run a timed mock interview (I’ll ask the first question now if you say "mock me for PhD Intern at Figma"). After each answer I’ll score and give one improvement and the next question.

One question: do you want me to run the timed mock now? (If yes, say “mock me for PhD Intern at Figma” and I’ll ask the first question.)
